task.title: TITLE-SENTINEL
task.prompt: A payments team plans to move the invoice export job from a nightly cron to an event-driven queue before the quarter closes on 30 November. Write a short plan covering the cut-over order, who signs off, and what happens to the 4,200 invoices already queued.
rubric: RULES-SENTINEL-1 uses the fixture-skill convention for plans
task.why_skill_matters: WHY-SENTINEL the skill wants a rollback section, quoted from SKILL.md

first_reply_items: Gives a cut-over order that moves the invoice export from the nightly cron to the queue in named steps.
States who signs off on the cut-over before the quarter closes on 30 November.
Says what happens to the 4,200 invoices already queued, for example drained first or replayed.

Explains the sequence in enough detail that a reader who has not seen the current cron setup could follow it: which job is switched off first, which consumer is switched on first, how the team confirms that the first batch of exported invoices matches what the nightly cron would have produced, and who is told when that check has passed or failed, including the finance contact who needs the files by the close.
Fits the steps before the quarter closes on 30 November.
Gives a way to go back to the nightly cron if the queue misbehaves.
